gap: No result ChatGPT got names or prices a screen extender, or says which kinds give two extended screens on an M3 MacBook Air with the lid open: a driver-based extender (FOPO S788 with FOPO's UsbDisplay driver, Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro with Mobile Pixels' own driver) or a driver-free dual extender plus a $119.99 DisplayLink adapter (Plugable USBC-6950M, plugable.com, 2026-11-21).
standout_why: Compared against Apple 117373 (cited), DisplayLink Manager First Time Configuration (cited; the 2026-11-21 fetch did not open, so its content comes from ChatGPT's summary), DeskExpander's MacBook Air M3 page, Macworld 675869 and Plugable's 2024-04-02 M3 Air blog. Apple says the second display 'will go dark or disconnect' when the lid opens and does not mention DisplayLink or extenders. DeskExpander says one display with the lid open and 'add DisplayLink for the second panel'. It names Mobile Pixels Trio, Geminos, Geminos X and Trio Max as not natively compatible but gives no prices and no driver route for those screens. Macworld and Plugable price only docks and adapters, with no screen extenders or portable monitors. No page prices an extender or connects a specific dual extender to a driver.
decides: This confirms the split ChatGPT's answer depends on. For one added screen, buy a native USB-C (DisplayPort Alt Mode) single panel: our Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS needs no driver. For two added screens with the lid open, the shopper needs a driver. The Trio 3 Pro runs both screens from one cable with Mobile Pixels' driver, but its maker-stated fit is 15–16 inch, which suits the 15-inch Air. The FOPO S788 uses the UsbDisplay driver, FOPO lists M3, and its fit range is 12–18.5 inch. The driver-free FOPO duals (S1, S7, S10, S11) lose on an M3 Air with the lid open unless a DisplayLink adapter is added, and whether each takes HDMI input for that adapter is not sourced. One caution: Macworld's Trio review says a standard M3 can set up both Trio screens without the driver, which conflicts with Apple's lid-open behaviour.
